result.topic: PAN-OS/Panorama Admin Role Profile behavior for API access — XML API granularity, REST API granularity, and least-privilege pattern for a read-only compliance-evidence collector service account

confirmedFacts.claim: The XML API tab in an Admin Role Profile only supports Enable/Disable per feature category — there is no Read Only state.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "For the XML API tab select, Enable or Disable." (Also confirmed on the reference help page docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/help/11-1/device/device-admin-roles: "Click the icons for specific XML API features to set the permitted access privileges (Enable or Disable).")

confirmedFacts.claim: The Web UI tab and the REST API tab both support three states per functional area: Enable, Read Only, or Disable.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "In the Web UI and REST API tabs, click the icon for each functional area to toggle it to the desired setting: Enable, Read Only or Disable." Corroborated identically on docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/help/11-1/device/device-admin-roles: "Click the icons for specific REST API features to set the permitted access privileges (Enable, Read Only, or Disable)."

confirmedFacts.claim: Enabling the XML API 'Config' permission grants get/show and set/edit/delete/rename/clone/move together — there is no separate read-only sub-toggle within Configuration, because the underlying schema models it as a single field with no read/write split.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Official Palo Alto Networks Go SDK (underlies the official Terraform provider). `type RoleDeviceXmlapi struct { Commit *string; Config *string; Export *string; Import *string; Iot *string; Log *string; Op *string; Report *string; UserId *string; ... }` and its XML-tag twin `type roleDeviceXmlapiXml struct { ... Config *string `xml:"config,omitempty"` ... }` — one flat string field per category, no nested get/set children anywhere in the struct.

confirmedFacts.claim: REST API admin-role permissions are modeled per INDIVIDUAL OBJECT TYPE (not just per broad Objects/Policies/Network/Device/System category), so REST access genuinely can be scoped to Read Only for one object type (e.g. SecurityRules) while another (e.g. NatRules) is Disabled — a granularity the flat 9-field XML API model cannot express.
confirmedFacts.evidence: `RoleDeviceRestapiPolicies` has 11 independent *string fields (ApplicationOverrideRules, AuthenticationRules, DecryptionRules, DosRules, NatRules, NetworkPacketBrokerRules, PolicyBasedForwardingRules, QosRules, SdwanRules, SecurityRules, TunnelInspectionRules). `RoleDeviceRestapiObjects` has 37 independent *string fields (Addresses, AddressGroups, AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles, UrlFilteringSecurityProfiles, Tags, Services, ... ). Each field carries its own XML tag (e.g. `xml:"security-rules,omitempty"`, `xml:"nat-rules,omitempty"`, `xml:"url-filtering-security-profiles,omitempty"`) and is settable independently of its siblings.

confirmedFacts.claim: Current (post-11.x) XML API category list is exactly 9 items: commit, config, export, import, iot, log, op, report, user-id.
confirmedFacts.evidence: `roleDeviceXmlapiXml` struct XML tags: commit, config, export, import, iot, log, op, report, user-id. This supersedes/extends the older 'only three explicitly named in prose' (Report, Log, Configuration) noted in earlier research — 'iot' in particular does not appear in older blog/doc enumerations, suggesting it's a newer addition.

confirmedFacts.claim: Palo Alto's own RBAC overview (pre-'iot' era) enumerates the XML API categories as Configuration, Commit, Import, Export, Operational Requests, User-ID Agent, Report, Log (8 total) — consistent with, and slightly older than, the SDK's 9-field current schema.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Page states PAN-OS Admin Roles assign these RBAC permission categories: Configuration, Commit, Import/Export, Operational Requests, User-ID Agent, Report, Log.

confirmedFacts.claim: Official recommended least-privilege pattern: use a dedicated, non-shared admin account for API access, and enable only the specific XML API feature categories actually needed rather than all of them.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "As a best practice, set up a separate admin account for XML API access." and "Select the XML API tab... Enable or disable XML API features from the list, such as Report, Log, and Configuration" — plus guidance to set an API key lifetime for rotation and to be able to revoke all keys.

confirmedFacts.claim: A genuinely platform-enforced read-only XML API mode DOES exist on the firewall — but only via the built-in dynamic admin role 'Superuser (read-only)', not via any custom Admin Role Profile. Trade-off: it grants read visibility to the ENTIRE box (not scoped to specific object types), unlike a custom profile.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Superuser (read-only): Read-only access to the firewall (enables the XML API in a read-only state)." No other dynamic role in the same list (Device administrator (read-only), Virtual system administrator (read-only)) carries this explicit XML-API-readonly parenthetical.

confirmedFacts.claim: On Panorama specifically, the dynamic role 'Superuser (read-only)' is documented with plainer wording ('Read-only access to Panorama') that omits the firewall page's explicit 'enables the XML API in a read-only state' phrasing — leaving it unconfirmed whether Panorama's version enforces the same XML-API-level guarantee or just WebUI/CLI read-only.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Panorama page lists 'Superuser' = 'Full read-write access to Panorama' and 'Superuser (read-only)' = 'Read-only access to Panorama', with no XML API parenthetical; separately, Panorama's 'Device Group and Template Administrator' custom Admin Role Profile type is described as having 'No access to the CLI or XML API' at all (that specific role type doesn't expose an XML API tab to enable/disable in the first place).

confirmedFacts.claim: A community/vendor integration write-up frames a practical least-privilege XML API role as 'enable all entries except Commit' — i.e. it treats disabling Commit (not Configuration) as the main lever, implicitly acknowledging Configuration itself carries write powers that can't be narrowed further within the XML API tab.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Disable all entries in the Web UI tab." / "Enable all entries except Commit in the XML API tab." (Broadcom-hosted mirror of a vendor integration guide, not Palo Alto's own docs — treat as corroborating, not authoritative.)

confirmedFacts.claim: REST API 'Read Only' is widely assumed to mean the object type's REST endpoint accepts GET only and rejects POST/PUT/DELETE, but no official page states this in explicit HTTP-verb terms in anything fetched during this research.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Doc only says the toggle sets access to 'Enable, Read Only or Disable' without spelling out which HTTP methods each state permits/blocks at the wire level.

remainingGaps: Literal enum strings PAN-OS accepts for REST API admin-role fields (e.g. exactly 'read-only' vs 'readonly' vs some other token) are not visible anywhere: the official pango SDK models every field as an untyped *string with no client-side enum validation (device-side validation only), and no official prose example was found showing a full <restapi> XML block with populated values. Needs a live device's /restapi-doc or a captured running-config XML dump.

Whether REST API 'Read Only' actually blocks POST/PUT/DELETE at the HTTP layer (vs. just hiding UI controls) is not explicitly documented in exact terms in any source found. Needs a live-device test: generate a key for a Read-Only-scoped role and attempt POST to e.g. /restapi/v11.0/Policies/SecurityRules, confirm 403/405.

Whether the 'Device administrator (read-only)' or 'Virtual system administrator (read-only)' dynamic roles carry the same platform-enforced 'read-only XML API' guarantee that official docs state explicitly only for 'Superuser (read-only)' is not confirmed either way — doc silence, not a stated negative.

Whether Panorama's 'Superuser (read-only)' dynamic role enforces XML-API read-only identically to the firewall's (the Panorama doc page omits the firewall page's explicit XML-API parenthetical) is unconfirmed — could be a documentation-wording gap rather than an actual behavioral difference. Needs live Panorama verification.

No Panorama-specific admin-role REST categories (e.g. device-group- or template-scoped resources) were found modeled in the official pango SDK's AdminRole schema — only firewall/vsys-scoped Device/Network/Objects/Policies/System fields exist. Unclear whether/how admin-role REST granularity applies when a Panorama REST call carries location=device-group, or whether it's governed by the same Objects/Policies fields regardless of location. Needs live Panorama /restapi-doc confirmation.

LIVEcommunity (community.paloaltonetworks.com / live.paloaltonetworks.com) blocked automated WebFetch with HTTP 403 on every attempt in this session, so despite being priority source #4 in the task instructions, no LIVEcommunity thread content could be directly quoted/verified firsthand — only WebSearch-engine snippets referencing such threads were available, and those are not citable as primary evidence.

The Broadcom-hosted claim that 'with Panorama 9.x+, XML API cannot be restricted to read-only' could not be re-located verbatim on direct WebFetch of the page it was attributed to (that page's actual quoted text was 'Enable all entries except Commit in the XML API tab', not the read-only-restriction sentence) — its exact source URL and wording remain unpinned.

No official page or SDK artifact was found that enumerates ALL REST API object-type fields per PAN-OS/Panorama version in one place outside the SDK source itself — field lists (Objects: 37 entries, Policies: 11 entries, Network: 34 entries) were only confirmable via the generated Go SDK, not via any single doc page; version-to-version differences in this list (e.g. for PAN-OS 11.1.13 vs 11.2.10-H3 specifically, Suncoast's actual fleet) were not checked against a live device or version-pinned schema dump.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: In Section 7, upgrade the citation for 'XML API tab only supports Enable/Disable, Configuration grants read+write together' from doc-prose-only to doc+official-SDK-confirmed by citing github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pango (device/adminrole/entry.go): the RoleDeviceXmlapi/roleDeviceXmlapiXml struct has exactly one flat `Config` string field with no nested get/set children, structurally proving there is no read-only sub-state to select even at the schema level, not just the GUI level.

Correct/qualify the blanket statement 'True platform-enforced read-only for XML API config access does not exist per the documented UI.' This is true only for CUSTOM Admin Role Profiles. Add a note that the built-in dynamic role 'Superuser (read-only)' is documented ('enables the XML API in a read-only state') to provide genuine platform-enforced read-only XML API access — worth evaluating as an alternative to a custom profile, but flag the trade-off explicitly: it grants full-box read visibility (not scoped to just License/Log/Config-get), which conflicts with least-privilege scoping unless Suncoast is fine with that breadth. Also note the same guarantee is NOT documented for Panorama's own Superuser (read-only) description, an open gap.

Replace the vague REST API recommendation ('set the relevant Objects/Policies categories to Read Only') with field-level specifics now confirmed to exist independently in the schema: set Policies.SecurityRules, Objects.UrlFilteringSecurityProfiles, and Objects.AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles each to Read Only individually, and leave every other REST object-type field (NatRules, Addresses, AddressGroups, Network.*, Device.*, System.Configuration, etc.) at Disabled — since the confirmed schema supports per-object-type granularity, a blanket 'Objects/Policies category' framing under-specifies the actual achievable least-privilege scope.

Update the XML API category enumeration from 'only three explicitly named in prose (Report, Log, Configuration)... full literal checkbox list not enumerated' to the SDK-confirmed complete current list: commit, config, export, import, iot, log, op, report, user-id (9 fields total, per github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pango device/adminrole/entry.go) — note 'iot' as a field not present in the older Ansible RBAC doc's 7-8-item enumeration, implying a newer PAN-OS-version addition worth flagging for live-version confirmation against Suncoast's 11.1.13/11.2.10-H3 fleet.
